## Implemented but untested (15)

| ID | Specification reference |
|---|---|
| HAL-018 | ACPI MADT: legacy/x2APIC processor entries, local NMI routes, I/O APIC routes, ISA overrides, and I/O APIC NMI sources decode from length-checked records |
| HAL-019 | APIC arithmetic: x2APIC MSRs, compressed TPR priority classes, timer divisors, and HPET-based counter calibration are checked |
| HAL-020 | HPET clocksource: 32-bit MMIO reads and wrap extension produce monotonic nanoseconds |
| HAL-021 | I/O APIC routes: GSI windows and ISA overrides are validated, redirections start masked, and NMI sources use MADT polarity/trigger flags |
| NVME-001 | NOLX M9 Controller capabilities: the queue size limit, doorbell stride, and ready timeout are decoded from their CAP fields, with the timeout in 500 ms units |
| NVME-002 | NOLX M9 Doorbells: each queue's submission and completion doorbells sit at 0x1000 plus (2 times the queue plus 0 or 1) times (4 shifted by the stride) |
| NVME-003 | NOLX M9 Enable and admin queue: CC enables the controller with 64-byte submission and 16-byte completion entries, CSTS.RDY reports ready, and AQA stores each admin queue size one less than the count, refusing sizes outside 1 to 4096 |
| NVME-004 | NOLX M9 Submission entry: the opcode and command identifier sit in dword 0, the namespace in dword 1, the data pointer in bytes 24 to 39, and the command dwords from byte 40; Identify carries its CNS value in dword 10 |
| NVME-005 | NOLX M9 I/O queue creation: Create I/O Completion Queue and Create I/O Submission Queue store the entry count one less, mark the queue physically contiguous, bind the submission queue to its completion queue, and refuse an empty or oversized queue |
| NVME-006 | NOLX M9 Read and write commands: the 64-bit LBA is split across dwords 10 and 11, the block count is stored one less in dword 12, and a zero-block transfer is refused |
| NVME-007 | NOLX M9 Completion entry: the command identifier, phase tag, status field, and submission queue head are read from their dwords, and the phase tag is not part of the status |
| NVME-008 | NOLX M9 Namespace: the block count comes from NSZE, and the block size comes from the format selected by FLBAS, refusing an exponent below 9 |
| NVME-009 | NOLX M9 Controller discovery: the probe finds the class 01:08:02 device, enables memory decoding and bus mastering, maps BAR 0, disables and re-enables the controller around the admin queue setup, identifies namespace 1, and reports its sector count and 512-byte block size |
| NVME-010 | NOLX M9 Polled sector read: sector 0 is read through I/O queue 1, the completion carries the command identifier with status zero, and the data matches the disk image's sector 0 |
| NVME-011 | NOLX M9 Polled round trip: a 2 KiB pattern is written to sectors 1600 to 1603 through I/O queue 1, the buffer is cleared, the sectors are read back, and the bytes are checked by CRC-32; CI checksums the same sectors in the NVMe disk copy after QEMU exits |

| MM-029 | mm | Page tables in the kernel: per-process address spaces are built over frames from the allocator | `tested-T2` | `AddressSpace::create_in_place` takes a zeroed PML4 from the frame allocator, marks it a page table, charges the system PTE pool, and shares the kernel half of the address space by copying the running root's PML4 entries from slot 256 up; everything below that is allocated and reclaimed by kernel/src/mm/tables.rs `KernelTableStore`, whose `release_table` returns an empty table to the frame allocator and releases its pool charge. The space is built *in place*, one field at a time, and torn down through a borrow: a value of the type is tens of kilobytes -- the boot self test found a stack overflow that had been silently writing past the kernel stack -- so nothing may move one through a function boundary. Teardown unmaps every range, frees the child tables the unmaps emptied, and frees the PML4. The boot self test proves the accounting closes: the page-table allocate/release counters move by the same amount across the test and the free-frame count returns to exactly its pre-test value, which is the `free frames A -> A; page tables allocated X -> Y, released X -> Y` part of the boot smoke's address-space assertion. (CI run 38125065287, revision 2e7279b) |

(CI run 38125065287, revision 2e7279b) |
| MM-032 | mm | Demand paging and copy-on-write: the four fault causes resolve against the VAD tree and the commit charge | `tested-T2` | kernel/src/mm/space::resolve implements the four causes of docs/architecture/03-memory-manager.md -- demand zero on a committed private page (the frame is zeroed before it is mapped and the test reads the zeroes back through the direct map), copy on write of a shared read-only page (`share_into` makes both spaces point at one frame read-only with a refcount of two; the child's write copies the frame, the copy carries the parent's byte, the two sides then move independently, and a write with no other owner re-protects in place instead of copying), a file-backed range refused until the Cache Manager exists (M7), and stack growth that extends a grow-down VAD by one page, coalesces the new descriptor back into the stack's own, demand-zeroes the new page, and refuses below the space's floor or beyond the growth limit -- and refuses an access in no VAD, a write to an `mprotect(PROT_READ)` page (a protection violation, not a copy), a fault on a guard page, and anything in the kernel half. kernel/src/hal/interrupts.rs routes vector 14 to it before the fatal report, so a resolvable fault returns to the faulting instruction. Boot line: `NOLX: address space selftest: 2 space(s), 4 VAD(s), 6 fault cause(s) resolved (3 demand-zero, 2 copy-on-write, 1 stack growth), 5 refusal(s); 6 page(s) mapped; free frames 121253 -> 121253; page tables allocated 0 -> 7, released 0 -> 7; system PTE peak 36 KiB; audit ok`. (CI run 38125065287, revision 2e7279b) |
| MM-033 | mm | Pool accounting in the kernel: the pools are charged from the boot log and reported through the object manager | `tested-T2` | The charging sites are inside the kernel: `mm::heap` takes a 256 KiB region against the nonpaged pool (`mm: kernel heap: 1 region(s), 256 KiB from the frame allocator, 256 KiB charged to the nonpaged pool`) and every page table and PML4 is charged to the system PTE pool, whose peak -- 36 KiB across the address-space self test -- is reported while every byte is released again. `kernel/src/obj/pool.rs` is the executive's view: `obj::pool::report` prints `obj: pool usage: nonpaged pool 256 KiB of 256 MiB (peak 256 KiB); paged pool 0 KiB of 64 MiB (peak 0 KiB); system PTE pool 0 KiB of 64 MiB (peak 0 KiB); nonpaged is illegal above PASSIVE, accounting ok`, which is the line the boot smoke asserts, and it runs `pool::check` while printing it. (CI run 38125065287, revision 2e7279b) |
| MM-034 | mm | NUMA node list: one buddy allocator per node and a zonelist that prefers the local node | `tested-T2` | The ordering rule is in nolx-mm-core `numa`: a node list with an ACPI-style distance matrix, a `zonelist` that puts the local node first and then the others by ascending distance with ties broken by identifier, offline nodes listed but never offered, and `check` for the invariants (duplicate, overlapping, and empty nodes are refused). Six host tests cover it. The kernel builds one node over the frames the frame map describes (`kernel/src/mm/numa.rs`), reports `mm: numa: 1 node(s), ..., local node 0, 121701 free frames, zonelist [0], distance matrix local=10`, and `mm::allocate_frames` now chooses the node by walking that zonelist before it allocates -- with one node that is one iteration, and a node that has no allocator refuses instead of taking memory from the wrong node. SRAT parsing (the source of a second node) is M9's ACPI work. (CI run 38125065287, revision 2e7279b) |
